trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at El Prat Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to the city center. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a relaxed walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — see Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside for free. Marvel at Gaudí's iconic facades without paying entry fees.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down to Plaça de Catalunya to get your bearings in the city. Head into the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) for a short exploratory walk through its medieval lanes. Grab a budget dinner near the hotel and wind down after a travel day.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or grab a coffee and croissant at a nearby café upon arrival (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Pick up a bocadillo (baguette sandwich) or slice of pizza from a takeaway near Eixample (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Bar Calders or a local tapas bar in Eixample — try patatas bravas, pan con tomate, and croquetas. Budget around €10–14 per person with a house wine

day_by_day.notes: August in Barcelona is hot (28–33°C typical). Stay hydrated, carry sunscreen, and wear light clothing. Validate your metro card — a T-Casual 10-trip card (€11.35) is great value for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Start early (before 9:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds at the iconic Sagrada Família. Book tickets online in advance (€26 basic entry, or €32 with tower access) — this is the one splurge worth every cent. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, studying the intricate facades and soaring interior columns bathed in colored light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes north to Park Güell. Entry to the Monumental Zone costs €10 (book online). Explore Gaudí's mosaic terraces and gingerbread gatehouses with panoramic views over the city. The surrounding park area outside the paid zone is free — great for photos and a picnic. After, head back toward Eixample and walk the elegant Passeig de Gràcia boulevard, window-shopping and photographing modernista architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Gràcia neighborhood (a short walk from Eixample) for the local evening atmosphere. Explore Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, popular with locals. As night falls, explore the bar scene in Gràcia — many bars offer free or cheap entry and lively outdoor terraces. Try a local craft beer at a Gràcia bar (€3–5 per beer).

meals.breakfast: Cafè de l'Acadèmia-style corner café near hotel — café amb llet (coffee with milk) and a tostada amb tomàquet (toast with tomato) for €3–5
meals.lunch: Picnic in Park Güell — grab supplies from a Mercadona or Lidl supermarket nearby: bread, cheese, jamón, fruit, and water for under €6
meals.dinner: La Pepita or a similar pintxos bar in Gràcia — pintxos (small bites on bread) are typically €1.50–2.50 each. Budget €10–13 for a satisfying dinner with a drink

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online at least a few days ahead — they sell out fast in August. Go to Sagrada Família right at opening (9:00 AM) to avoid the worst of the heat and queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana, a stunning UNESCO-listed modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Guided tours cost €22 (or €18 if booked online). Alternatively, if budget is tight, admire the ornate exterior for free and peek at the foyer. Afterward, explore the El Born neighborhood on foot — a trendy, artsy district full of independent shops and beautiful streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Barceloneta Beach (free entry) — a 20-minute walk or short metro ride from El Born. Spend a couple of hours swimming in the Mediterranean. Walk along the Passeig Marítim beachfront promenade. Visit the nearby Port Olímpic area to see the striking copper Fish sculpture by Frank Gehry (free to view). Explore the waterfront and the Barceloneta neighborhood's grid of narrow streets.
day_by_day.evening: As the sun sets, head back toward El Born or the Gothic Quarter. Visit the free outdoor space of Plaça Reial — a grand neoclassical square with palm trees and Gaudí-designed lampposts. This square comes alive at night with bars and restaurants. For nightlife, El Born and the Gothic Quarter are buzzing by 10:00–11:00 PM. Try a cocktail at one of the many bars (€7–10). Barcelona nightlife starts late — clubs don't fill until midnight or later.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in El Born or a local bakery — croissant, coffee, and fresh orange juice for €5–7
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) at a local restaurant in Barceloneta or El Born — typically €11–14 for a 3-course meal with bread and a drink. This is the best budget value in Barcelona
meals.dinner: Grab a slice of pizza or a falafel wrap from a takeaway near the Gothic Quarter (€4–7) so you have more money for drinks during the evening out

day_by_day.notes: Barceloneta Beach is crowded in August — go in the afternoon when many tourists are sightseeing. Watch your belongings on the beach and in the Gothic Quarter, as pickpocketing is common in tourist areas. Bring a padlock for your bag.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (L3 green line) to Paral·lel and then the free funicular up to Montjuïc hill. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (€14 entry) — a world-class modern art museum in a beautiful rationalist building. Even if modern art isn't your primary interest, the architecture and hilltop setting are worth the visit. Alternatively, walk around Montjuïc for free — the hilltop has incredible panoramic views over Barcelona, the port, and the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Montjuïc Castle (exterior free; interior €5) with sweeping 360-degree views. Walk through the Jardins de Laribal (free ornamental gardens on the hillside). Head back down via the Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car (€12.70 round trip) for spectacular aerial views — or take the free funicular back down to save money. In the afternoon, visit the Mercat de Sant Antoni in Eixample (free to browse) — a beautifully restored 19th-century iron market with food stalls, vintage books, and local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Tonight is your big nightlife night. Eixample's 'Gayxample' area (around Carrer del Consell de Cent) has some of Barcelona's best bars and is welcoming to all. Start with pre-drinks (pres) from a supermarket (cava bottle ~€3–5) in the hotel or a park — a classic Barcelona tradition called 'botellón.' Hit the bars around 11:00 PM. Clubs like Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz (€12–18 entry, often includes one drink) are legendary Barcelona venues for live music and electronic music. Expect to stay out until 3:00–5:00 AM.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh croissant de mantequilla and café solo from a neighborhood bakery (€2–4). Many bakeries open by 7:30–8:00 AM
meals.lunch: Mercat de Sant Antoni food stalls or a nearby menú del día restaurant in Eixample — budget €10–13
meals.dinner: Light dinner before the night out — bocadillo from a bar or a burger from a local spot (€6–9). Eat late by Spanish standards (9:00–10:00 PM) to align with the local rhythm

day_by_day.notes: For the nightlife evening, wear comfortable shoes — you'll be on your feet for hours. Bring only a small amount of cash and a card. Most Barcelona clubs are free or cheap before midnight, then charge entry after. Check for flyers around El Born and Gràcia for free-entry promotions.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from the late night! Have a slow morning — pick up fresh pastries from a local forn de pa (bakery) and enjoy breakfast at a leisurely pace. Once ready, visit the Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau — a stunning UNESCO-listed hospital complex designed by Domènech i Montaner, often considered even more beautiful than Sagrada Família. Entry is €16 (€14 online). It's a short walk from Sagrada Família along the Avinguda de Gaudí.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to La Boqueria Market on La Rambla (free to enter and browse) — one of Europe's most famous food markets. Sample fresh fruit, jamón, and local cheeses. Be aware that stalls on the edges are cheaper than those at the center. Walk the full length of La Rambla from Plaça de Catalunya to the Columbus Monument (free) at the port. Visit the Barri Gòtic one last time — explore the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 PM or after 5:30 PM, otherwise €9) and the hidden Plaça de Sant Felip Neri.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample near your hotel. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget meal — try a local Catalan restaurant for pa amb tomàquet, escalivada, and a glass of local Penedès wine. After dinner, take one final walk along Passeig de Gràcia at night when the modernista buildings are beautifully lit. End the evening with a nightcap at a rooftop bar — many Eixample hotels have rooftop bars open to the public with views of the city lights (cocktails €9–12).

meals.breakfast: Slow hotel-area breakfast — coffee and pastries from a local forn (€4–6)
meals.lunch: La Boqueria Market snacks and fresh fruit (€6–10) — try a fresh juice, a jamón bocadillo, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Local Catalan restaurant in Eixample — 2-course meal with wine, budget €18–25 per person for a proper farewell dinner. Look for restaurants on side streets off Passeig de Gràcia for better prices

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags the night before if flying out the next morning. Keep your T-Casual metro card if it has trips remaining for the airport journey. La Boqueria is extremely crowded in August — go before 11:00 AM or after 4:00 PM for a more pleasant experience. Avoid buying full meals at La Boqueria as they are overpriced — use it for snacking and browsing only.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Explore Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica with a guided tour that reveals the intricate architectural details, symbolism, and history of this UNESCO World Heritage Site. Book a tower access ticket for panoramic views of the city.

experiences.description: Discover Gaudí's colorful mosaic wonderland with a self-guided walk through Park Güell. Admire the dragon staircase, Hypostyle Room, and sweeping city-to-sea views. Arrive early to beat the crowds and enjoy the surreal landscape in golden morning light.

experiences.name: Opium Beach Club Night
experiences.description: Experience Barcelona's legendary beachfront nightlife at Opium, one of the most iconic open-air clubs situated directly on Barceloneta Beach. Dance to international DJs, enjoy signature cocktails, and soak in the electric Mediterranean atmosphere until sunrise.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Travel from airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud (approx. 35–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll the iconic Passeig de Gràcia, just steps from the hotel. Admire the 'Block of Discord' featuring Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller from the outside — a perfect low-key introduction to Eixample's Modernista architecture. Browse local shops and soak in the neighborhood vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Head to El Born neighborhood for the El Born Tapas & Bar Crawl. Wander through narrow medieval streets sampling pintxos, jamón, and patatas bravas paired with craft cocktails and local vermouth at a series of buzzing bars. A great way to ease into Barcelona's late-night culture.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or a quick café stop near the hotel upon arrival — try Federal Café on Carrer del Parlament for a relaxed welcome bite.
meals.lunch: Light meal at a casual Eixample café after check-in — try Bar Calders on Carrer del Parlament for a classic bocadillo and draft beer.
meals.dinner: Included in the El Born Tapas & Bar Crawl — budget €25–35 per person across multiple stops including El Xampanyet for cava and tapas, and Bar del Pla for modern Catalan pintxos.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day is intentionally relaxed. Keep luggage light for the evening outing. El Born is about a 20-minute walk or short metro ride (L4) from Eixample. Bars in El Born typically get lively from 21:00 onwards — embrace the Spanish late dining culture.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Book the first morning slot (9:00 or 10:00) to beat the crowds. The guided tour reveals the breathtaking symbolism of Gaudí's unfinished basilica, including the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like nave, and the towers. Allow 1.5–2 hours. The basilica is a 15-minute walk from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell Self-Guided Architecture Walk — Take the Metro L3 or a short taxi to Park Güell. Explore Gaudí's colorful mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and the winding pathways with panoramic views over the city. The self-guided format lets you linger at your own pace. Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for a relaxed dinner, then experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife at Opium Beach Club. Head down to Barceloneta around 23:00 when the open-air club comes alive with music, sea breezes, and a vibrant crowd.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Forn de Sant Josep bakery near Sagrada Família for a traditional Catalan breakfast of pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) and coffee — €5–8.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Park Güell or grab a bite at one of the park's nearby casual eateries. Alternatively, try La Pepita on Carrer de Montmany for creative montaditos — €12–18.
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved Eixample institution for tapas and cold beer. Expect to queue slightly; worth it. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Sagrada Família tickets online well in advance — they often sell out weeks ahead. Park Güell's monumental zone also requires timed entry tickets (€10). Wear comfortable shoes for both. Opium has no strict dress code but smart-casual is recommended; entry is typically free before midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) — Wander the labyrinthine medieval streets, visiting the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and the Roman ruins of the Temple d'August (free entry). This neighborhood is a living architectural timeline from Roman to Gothic to Baroque. Allow a leisurely 2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Chiringuito Dining — Head to Barceloneta Beach for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathing. The beach is a short walk from the Gothic Quarter. Rent a sun lounger, enjoy the Mediterranean atmosphere, and dine at a beachfront chiringuito for fresh seafood and sangria as the sun begins to lower.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Port Olímpic waterfront, then enjoy a cocktail at one of the marina bars. For a mid-range nightlife option, check out Shôko or Pacha Barcelona near the waterfront for a more relaxed club experience compared to Opium.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia near the Gothic Quarter — a charming spot for coffee and a full Catalan breakfast with eggs and cold cuts — €8–12.
meals.lunch: Chiringuito dining at Barceloneta Beach — order grilled fish, gambas al ajillo, and a cold Estrella Damm at La Cova Fumada or Chiringuito Escribà. Budget €20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: La Mar Salada near Barceloneta — excellent mid-range seafood restaurant known for its paella and fresh catch. Reservations recommended. Budget €30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: August in Barcelona is peak summer — Barceloneta Beach will be busy. Arrive by 14:00 to secure a good spot. Keep valuables secure on the beach. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes on the cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana — Take a guided tour of this UNESCO-listed Modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The stained-glass ceiling and ornate facades are jaw-dropping. Tours run from 10:00 and last about 55 minutes. Located in Sant Pere, a short walk from El Born.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc Hill — Take the cable car or funicular up to Montjuïc for stunning panoramic views of the city and port. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (€14 entry) for world-class modern art, and stroll the gardens of the Jardins de Laribal. A peaceful contrast to the busy city below.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for a classic Barcelona evening — aperitivo hour at a rooftop bar. Try the rooftop of Hotel Majestic or Dry Martini bar on Carrer d'Aribau, a legendary cocktail institution. End the night with a late dinner in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: El Nacional on Passeig de Gràcia — a beautifully restored food market hall with multiple breakfast options from pastries to full plates — €8–15.
meals.lunch: Bodega Sepúlveda near Montjuïc — a traditional no-frills bodega with a €12 menú del día including wine. Authentic and affordable.
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza on Carrer de Londres — a beloved Eixample spot for creative Neapolitan-style pizzas in a cool industrial space. Perfect mid-range evening meal — €15–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Palau de la Música tickets should be booked online in advance. The Montjuïc cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) offers spectacular views but can have queues in August — consider going mid-afternoon. Dry Martini bar is a Barcelona institution; reservations for a table are recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) — Splurge on a proper interior visit to one of Gaudí's masterpiece buildings on Passeig de Gràcia, both a short walk from the hotel. Casa Batlló's dragon-scale rooftop and bone-like facade are surreal; La Pedrera's rooftop warriors are iconic. Choose one and allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mercat de Sant Antoni — A beautifully restored 19th-century iron market in Eixample, now a vibrant food and lifestyle market. Browse fresh produce, grab artisan snacks, and soak up the local atmosphere. Nearby, explore the charming streets of Sant Antoni neighborhood, Barcelona's hippest new district.
day_by_day.evening: Final night send-off — Return to Barceloneta for a last sunset dinner by the sea, then head to Opium Beach Club or CDLC (Carpe Diem Lounge Club) for a proper Barcelona farewell night out. Dance until late under the stars with the Mediterranean as your backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Alsur Café on Carrer del Consell de Cent — a bright, modern café perfect for a leisurely final-morning breakfast with avocado toast and specialty coffee — €10–15.
meals.lunch: Mercat de Sant Antoni food stalls — graze on fresh oysters, charcuterie, and local cheeses with a glass of cava. Budget €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Barraca on the Barceloneta waterfront — stunning seafront location with excellent rice dishes and fresh seafood. A memorable final dinner. Budget €35–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Casa Batlló or La Pedrera tickets online — both are popular and sell out fast in August. If budget allows, the Casa Batlló Magic Nights evening experience (€49) combines architecture with a rooftop show and is a unique splurge. Pack light for the final evening out as you may be heading to the airport early the following morning.

meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel or a quick gourmet bite at Parking Pizza or Cervecería Catalana near Eixample upon arrival
meals.dinner: Disfrutar — avant-garde tasting menu with wine pairing (reserve well in advance)

The basilica is a short taxi or metro ride from Eixample. Allocate 2–3 hours to fully absorb the intricate facades and soaring interior.

day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Lasarte (3 Michelin stars, Chef Martín Berasategui) for an extraordinary Basque-influenced fine dining experience. Post-dinner, head to the rooftop terrace of the Ohla Eixample hotel for cocktails with skyline views before a relaxed early night.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or visit Federal Café in Eixample for specialty coffee and avocado toast
meals.lunch: La Pepita Lunch — a charming gourmet sandwich and natural wine bar near Park Güell in Gràcia district
meals.dinner: Lasarte — three Michelin star tasting menu with sommelier-guided wine pairing

Sample fresh produce, artisan cheeses, and cured meats. Then explore the medieval Gothic streets of El Born on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Chiringuito Dining — Take a taxi or leisurely walk down to Barceloneta beach. Spend the afternoon on a premium sunbed reservation (arranged through your hotel concierge). Dine at a high-end chiringuito such as La Cova Fumada or Agua Restaurant for fresh seafood with ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Opium Beach Club Night — Experience Barcelona's legendary open-air beachfront nightclub. Arrange VIP table service through your hotel concierge for priority entry and a reserved table. The club typically peaks between midnight and 4:00 AM — pace yourself with dinner beforehand.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Parking Coffee or Nomad Coffee Lab in El Born — specialty coffee and pastries
meals.lunch: Chiringuito lunch at Agua Restaurant on Barceloneta beachfront — grilled fish, paella, and sangria
meals.dinner: Pre-club dinner at Bestial, an upscale Mediterranean restaurant beneath the Hotel Arts with terrace sea views

day_by_day.notes: VIP table booking at Opium is strongly recommended in August — contact the hotel concierge immediately. Dress code is smart-casual to elegant. Bring a light layer for the sea breeze late at night.

day_by_day.morning: Late, leisurely start after the previous night's clubbing. Enjoy a luxurious in-hotel breakfast. Mid-morning visit to Casa Batlló — book the Magic Nights premium evening experience or the daytime guided tour with AR glasses for an immersive architectural deep-dive into Gaudí's masterpiece. Located directly on Passeig de Gràcia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private architecture tour of Eixample's Modernista gems — hire a specialist guide to explore Palau del Baró de Quadras, Casa Comalat, and Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau (a UNESCO World Heritage hospital complex). Return to hotel for a spa session or rooftop pool time.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at El Nacional's rooftop or the Terraza del Claris hotel. Then dinner at Moments (2 Michelin stars, inside Mandarin Oriental) for refined Catalan haute cuisine. End the night with a sophisticated jazz session at Jamboree Jazz Club in the Gothic Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent in-hotel breakfast — request a room-service spread or visit the hotel's dining room
meals.lunch: Light gourmet lunch at Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — premium tapas and craft beer
meals.dinner: Moments at Mandarin Oriental — Catalan tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Casa Batlló tickets online. The Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau is one of Barcelona's most underrated architectural gems — allow 90 minutes. Spa at the hotel should be reserved in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning stroll along Passeig de Gràcia for last-minute luxury shopping — Loewe, Massimo Dutti flagship, and local design boutiques. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies (housed in a stunning modernist building) for a curated contemporary art experience if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Barcelona Boutique Stay. Enjoy a farewell lunch at Bodega Sepúlveda, a beloved Eixample wine bar with natural wines and seasonal Catalan small plates. Private luxury transfer to Barcelona–El Prat Airport with ample time before departure.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor it slowly
meals.lunch: Bodega Sepúlveda — natural wines, charcuterie, and Catalan seasonal dishes
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight (arrange airport lounge access — El Prat's VIP lounge is recommended)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm late check-out with the hotel to maximize your final morning. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for the airport transfer and security in August peak season. Pack any food souvenirs (cured meats, olive oil, cava) in checked luggage.
